abstract: Systematic meta-analysis enables cumulative science, but expert-led, manual workflows do not scale with the growing literature. In neuroimaging, automated frameworks are widely used but typically sacrifice precision by using coarse article selection and pooling reported results, combining different tasks, populations or comparisons even when only a subset is relevant. Here we present AutoNIMA, a large language model (LLM)-guided framework that screens articles using expert-defined eligibility criteria and parses heterogeneous tables to extract brain stereotactic coordinates and select relevant analyses within each article. AutoNIMA produced maps more closely matching expert-curated references than a search-only baseline representing existing automated methods in 26 of 27 meta-analyses. Analysis-level selection accounted for most of the improvement. These findings demonstrate how LLM-guided curation can filter relevant analyses within the same paper and support scalable neuroimaging evidence synthesis.
